subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should memory-core dreaming be agent-isolated by default for agents sharing one workspace, or should the accepted fix be an opt-in `dreaming.agents` allowlist like https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057?
rationale: Current main still pools shared-workspace agents, while the active fix candidate adds new configuration and compatibility behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Default Agent Isolation
options.body: Make each dreaming run ingest only the owning agent's sessions by default, treating cross-agent pooling as unsafe unless a future explicit sharing contract exists.

options.title: Opt-In Allowlist
options.body: Accept the PR's config-gated agent selection as the compatibility-preserving path, then document that operators must configure scoped dreaming in shared-workspace fleets.

options.title: Document Workspace Pooling
options.body: Declare workspace-level pooling expected behavior and close the bug only if maintainers intentionally accept the privacy and identity tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Default Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Make each dreaming run ingest only the owning agent's sessions by default, treating cross-agent pooling as unsafe unless a future explicit sharing contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned and already framed the key shared-workspace design question in the issue discussion.
